intro: The home page says every word of Scripture on this site is public domain. That is a claim, so here is the chain behind it. For each hosted text: the file the site ingested, the rights record that says it is free, what the processing did to it, and where it serves in the reader. Nothing here is copied from a modern copyrighted translation.

boundary: Modern copyrighted translations are discussed in the ledger and the cases. They are never hosted as text.
The original-language editions and their morphology are openly licensed, not public domain. Their attribution and change notices travel with the data.
Wikisource and CCEL are transcriptions of public-domain works. A transcription adds no new copyright to the words, which is why the chain ends at the 1913 volume rather than at a website.
Chapter guides, book briefings, and the search indexes are this site's own work built on the hosted texts. They are not Scripture text and make no claim to be.
